items.title: 01版 - “赣小橙”的兴农路
items.content:
2026年11月28日

赣南初冬，连片丘陵披上金黄。江西省赣州市信丰县大塘埠镇长岗村的正大橙园里，山风一吹，果香扑鼻。

“咔嚓”一声，一颗名叫“赣小橙”的脐橙被果农从枝头剪下，从这里出发，将踏上一段新旅程。这段旅程，一头连着一条年产值超230亿元、品牌价值近700亿元的产业链，一头连着上百万老区群众的幸福生活。

赣南脐橙树，曾是帮老区拔掉穷根的“当家树”。

2023年10月，习近平总书记在江西考察时强调：“坚持产业兴农、质量兴农、绿色兴农，把农业建设成为大产业，加快建设农业强省。”

赣南脐橙，正是殷殷嘱托在红土地上最甜的回响。

曾经，无论丰年灾年，果农心中多有担忧：怕灾年减产、怕丰产压价、怕质量参差、怕市场起伏……

硕果飘香时节，跟着“赣小橙”走出果园，走过分选线、加工厂和出海口，能够看到赣南老区脐橙产业的“三级跳”：跳出“看天吃饭”的被动，跳出“卖原果”的低端，跳出“内销内卷”的局限。一步步化解发展中的烦恼，塑造乡村全面振兴的新优势。

**第一站：老果园里的新起点**

刚离枝的“赣小橙”，被装进果筐。接下来的路，不用自己“走”。

无人机吊着果子越过缓坡，两分钟便轻巧落在运输车前。

果子长得饱满，秘密藏在中控室里。

信丰县正大农业发展有限公司总经理肖蒋标，正在盯着他的“新农具”：屏幕上，水肥、虫情、气象数据跳动。管道顺着丘陵蜿蜒起伏。轻点手机，细密的防病电解水雾弥漫林间，宛如仙境。

“过去要15个人干3天的活，现在3个多小时就收工。”肖蒋标笑言。

一颗果子，在赣南老区接力种了半个多世纪。

老区丘陵多、水田少，荒山种不出庄稼，要拔掉穷根就得另找出路。

1970年，在信丰安西园艺场任技术员的袁守根，赴湖南邵阳选购柑橘苗木。听说当地从国外引进了新品种脐橙，品质好，但挂果率低。

“能不能试试？”袁守根选下一批树苗，扛回信丰。

选了一块朝南向阳的小山包，把苗栽下去，袁守根就在旁边搭起棚子，建起“哨岗”，日复一日观察、记录。

控制夏梢、提高着果率，山地套种绿肥……第三年，156株树苗挂果，次年收获约200公斤。

1976年，20颗脐橙被送到广交会试销，香港客商一眼看中。随后，在香港市场，每公斤脐橙卖出36港元的高价。

在袁守根的带动下，县里将脐橙发展作为示范产业。县领导带着党员干部下地示范种苗，不断引育，终于选出适合红土地的当家品种。“赣小橙”的祖辈，扎下了根。

上世纪90年代，“山上再造”“兴果富民”号角吹响，引导老区群众种橙脱贫。1992年，肖蒋标的叔伯看到先种的人家盖起小洋楼，也扛锄头上山，从15亩起步，种下这片果园的第一批橙树。

2012年，《国务院关于支持赣南等原中央苏区振兴发展的若干意见》出台，明确提出支持脐橙等特色产业发展。

这一年，在外创业的肖蒋标回到信丰，接手老果园，扩种到2000亩。买苗有补贴，买农机有补助，政策一路托举。他请来袁守根做顾问，红火时年产400万斤。

然而，一场危机不期而至——黄龙病来了。

这种病靠木虱传播，染上后只能砍树。2022年，肖蒋标的2000亩果树全砍了。

面对推倒重来的困境，老区没有认输。为帮助果农重建家园，中央和省市财政累计投入超5亿元专项资金防控黄龙病。

“砍掉病树、重新买苗都有补贴，市里还引导果农联防联控、推广无毒苗木。”肖蒋标介绍。

2023年，肖蒋标种下新苗，宽行窄株高起垄，方便机械化操作；1/3果树选育“赣脐5号”早熟品种，比普通脐橙早20天上市。今年第一年挂果，每棵树产量可达三四十斤。

这一代“赣小橙”，比过去长得更壮了。

**第二站：流水线上的新身价**

眼下正值上市旺季，装满“赣小橙”的果筐，被卡车拖进了果园边的正大农业发展有限公司脐橙分选厂。

机械臂翻转果筐，橙子“哗啦”一下铺满流水线。清洗、刷干、杀菌，“洗澡”后，“赣小橙”们在4个通道上排着队，迎来体检环节。

滚轮上，几十个摄像头连续闪烁，看出它果面光洁、色泽均匀，横径82毫米，是个标准的“2L”号果。前方的电子秤动态称重，果大分量足。再往前，是近红外光谱“CT扫描”，光线一打，直接看透果肉，测出“赣小橙”糖度高达14.2%。

现场，48个分选出口全开，几吨重的橙子如流水般穿梭。中控室的电脑后台正飞速测算每一颗果子的综合得分。

得分一出，果托“啪”的一声，将“赣小橙”精准拨进“特级果”出口。

“这套算法，其实是在执行新国标。”看着屏幕上跳跃的数据，肖蒋标说，“好果子终于能证明自己了。”

说起脐橙分级，赣州市果业发展中心副主任温明生如数家珍：最早只有统货，俗称“一树下”，后来按大小重量分、能识别果皮瑕疵。但糖度藏在里面，只能切开抽样或凭经验估。碰上大年，客商一句“不够甜”，就把整车果压到1.2元一斤，果农只能干瞪眼。

痛点，逼出了装备升级。

“赣小橙”用的“体检”设备，来自本地企业绿萌科技股份有限公司。公司董事长朱壹果农出身，深知痛点，带着团队跨界转型，造分选机。

为了让更多果园买得起分选设备，市级财政先补贴，又帮助纳入国家和省级农机补贴目录。目前，绿萌设备为80%的赣南脐橙做分选，市场份额国内第一。

机器跑多了，积累的海量数据，成为修订新标准的底气。

“由市果业发展中心牵头起草的《脐橙》新国标，今年7月1日起实施，顺应了产业从‘看颜值’向‘重品质’的科学转变。”温明生说，把糖度等内在指标拉高，也倒逼果农种出好果子。

修订国标之前，经过了小范围市场试水。赣州联合深圳开展质量分级试点，两地互认标准。拿到“A+”级评定的果子，可直接进驻深圳高端商超，售价比普通果高出30%——给“赣小橙”发了一张直通粤港澳大湾区市场的“品质身份证”。

流水线尽头，特级果“赣小橙”，零售一斤最高卖到8元。带着这个新身价，它即将走出大山，走向广阔市场。

**第三站：岔路口前的新赛道**

做完“体检”，那些个头偏小、其貌不扬的等外果“兄弟们”和“赣小橙”走到了分别的岔路口。

以前，它们常面临“卖不掉、卖不好”的困境。仅赣南，每年就有约40万吨的等外果被拉去马路边贱卖。

但这次，“兄弟们”坐上运输车，远赴70公里外的安远县，开启了一场“重生”之旅。

在江西果然食品有限公司，50台自动削皮机同时开工，帮果子脱掉黄色的“外衣”，实现果皮分离。

过去被当废料扔掉的果皮，现在成了香饽饽。

皮切成丁，倒入大铁罐，启动冷冻皮油分离——水渣结冰沉底，橙油浮在冰面。这便是能加工成香精、香水的毛油。

“一天处理1000吨脐橙，能提取两吨毛油，光这一项就能卖20万元！”公司董事长欧阳军指着铁罐说。

脱了“外衣”的果球在产线上继续翻滚，机械爪灵巧剥瓣，撕开白色“瓣衣”。瓣衣可提取果胶，肉囊可提取膳食纤维——曾经的边角料，现在一吨都在四五百元。

而透亮的橙汁，则进入零下40摄氏度的大冰库，微冰晶闪冻技术让它在5秒内结成橙冰，迅速锁鲜，去往头部商超和新茶饮品牌。

这便是“五分离、五重构”的技术魔法，让脐橙浑身是宝。“我们已把研发拓展到烘焙、馅料、冷饮等十大行业，开发出橙饼干、色拉酱等多款高附加值产品。”欧阳军说。

至此，等外果完成了“重生”。收进来每吨1000元，深加工后值5940元，身价一路追赶“赣小橙”。

今年，果然食品还拿下了国家优势特色产业集群项目，分3年获530万元中央财政资金支持，从研发到加工如虎添翼。

从鲜果的20%利润率，到深加工50%以上的利润率，不仅消化了滞销果、挖潜增收，还提升了产业的抗风险韧性。如今，赣南的深加工企业已有27家，助力脐橙实现“季产年销”。

这条现代化产业链，红利为老区人所共享。

安远县鹤子镇果农郭祥华，种了320棵脐橙树，往年总有一两万斤等外果卖不上价。2023年，他加入果然食品订单保价收购体系，每年等外果这一项就能增收6000多元。农闲时，老郭还会进果然务工“挣外快”。

果然食品的150名员工中，既有返乡女工，也有老郭这样种完橙就进厂的季节工。企业以订单保底价收果，带动5000多户农户户均年增收5000元以上。仅安远县，脐橙产业链已带动16万人就业创业。

从“卖果子”到“卖品牌”“卖精加工”，岔路口上，脐橙“兄弟们”的出路更宽了。

**第四站：报关单上的新舞台**

“画面放大，重点看果箱内部……”

龙南海关视频会议室，大屏正切换着各地果园抽检画面。屏幕这头是“云端”查验，镜头一转，几十公里外的正大农业脐橙分选厂，海关查验人员熟练地开箱、核对后，一份检验检疫电子底账随即生成。

“100万斤，准备发往俄罗斯！”肖蒋标坐在电脑前，打开国际贸易单一窗口，指尖轻点，报关完成。这是正大农业首次敲开俄罗斯市场大门。

为了让鲜果抢“鲜”出国，海关开辟了绿色通道，推行“5+2”预约查检。

“周六预约，周日工作人员就上门了。”出国手续办妥，“赣小橙”整装待发，肖蒋标为它预约了3天后从赣州国际陆港出发的中欧班列。

得益于江西内陆开放型经济试验区建设，从赣州国际陆港出发，出海更快、成本更低。“批发出口价每斤3元，到了俄罗斯的商超，身价还能翻倍！”肖蒋标说。

过去，不少小果园因为规模小，很难拿到出口订单。去年开始，龙南海关创新推出“1+N”集群注册模式。正大农业作为“龙头果园”，带着周边200多家小果园一起干，统一种植标准、共享出口资质……目前，已有6家小果园拿到了出海“通行证”。

跟着“赣小橙”一起跨海越洋的“发小们”，越来越多了。2025年，龙南海关辖区赣南脐橙出口量达2.31万吨，同比增长77%；今年前10个月，出口量2.29万吨，同比增长1.2倍，足迹遍布24个国家和地区。

远赴海外的“赣小橙”乘风破浪，留在国内的“手足”同样精彩。

在龙南，乡镇基层党组织带领果农创新跨界融合消费场景，南武当山景区旁，南亨脐橙场成为许多游客打卡点，挑果、尝鲜、观景，高峰期一周接待超3000人次；桃江乡马槽山脐橙园，城里人花1380元认领一棵树当“橙主”，600多棵树被抢认。

在更广阔的市场端，电商销售已占三成多。溯源直播、网红带货等新手段层出不穷。“主攻城市营销”正火热：赣州18个县区各自锁定目标，深耕全国36个大中城市。龙南市主攻哈尔滨市场，从最初当地人“没听说过赣南脐橙”，到现在一年卖出500万斤。

从老党员带头试种第一棵苗，到政策一路托举。目前种植面积达190万亩、种果农户超13万户的百亿大产业，赣南脐橙的每一次跨越，都写着老区群众的韧劲与红土地的沧桑巨变。

items.title: 谷歌发布新一代 TPU，开发者：真正重要的不是芯片
items.content:
Google Cloud 已开源 TPU Sync。这是一个原生 C++ 库，可以在 TPU HBM、主机 DRAM、共享存储和数据中心网络之间传输 KV 缓存块与模型权重。GCP 还发布了 TPU 8tx 和 TPU 8i Max 系统。该项目主要面向两类加速器经常因等待数据而闲置的工作负载：长上下文和解耦式大语言模型服务，以及将训练器更新后的权重推送至 Rollout 采样器的强化学习循环。

在 Prefill 和 Decode 解耦场景中，Google 表示，Qwen3 235B 的 KV 缓存传输延迟中位数从数秒降至约 230 毫秒。在低并发情况下，该模型的平均首 Token 延迟（TTFT）降低了 60%，另一款 480B 模型则降低了 90%。在前缀缓存场景中，Google 报告称，64K 上下文工作负载的平均 TTFT 最多可降低 90%。

开发者可以获得适用于 JAX 和 PyTorch 的 Python Wheel，其中包含 KV 缓存管理器、KV Store 和权重同步器 API。TPU Sync 通过 vLLM 的 KVConnector 接口充当 vLLM-TorchTPU 的 KV Connector，同时也是 SGLang-TorchTPU 的解耦服务和分层缓存后端，并可与 GKE 上的 llm-d 1.0 配合，实现感知前缀缓存的路由。适用于 Pathways 和多控制器 JAX 的强化学习权重同步模块仍处于实验阶段。GitHub 代码仓库已经吸收了此前的 TPU Raiden 代码库。仓库警告称，API 正在快速变化，PyPI 上目前只有开发版本，因此建议固定使用最近一个已知可用的提交。该项目已在 TPU v7x 和 v6e 上通过验证，PyTorch Wheel 则需要与之匹配的 `torch_tpu` 构建版本，而该版本尚未发布到公共软件包索引。

在 GPU 上，类似问题通常由 NVIDIA Dynamo 及其 NIXL 传输库处理；LMCache 可以将 KV 缓存卸载到 CPU 内存、磁盘或远程存储；Mooncake 是月之暗面 Kimi 背后以 KVCache 为核心的服务架构；vLLM 自身也提供了解耦式 Prefill Connector。TPU Sync 的主要区别在于，它与 PJRT 和 TPU Tile 布局深度绑定，并且在同一个库中同时覆盖了强化学习权重传输。

早期讨论更多聚焦于数据移动，而不是新芯片。开发者 Anand Butani 分享道：

相比芯片的名字，TPU Sync 将 KV 缓存传输延迟降低 90% 对我来说更重要。长上下文服务的大部分瓶颈，都出在跨节点移动缓存上。

另一位以 @lgoodbookd 为笔名发帖的开发者进行了一番粗略计算，说明为什么单靠带宽无法解决这个问题：

8i Max 将 HBM 带宽翻倍至约 17.2 TB/s，但在一个 235B MoE 模型上，单个 64K 会话仍会占用约 12.6 GB 的 KV 缓存。这就是为什么开源 TPU Sync（主机 DRAM KV 分层存储，每台 v7x 主机约 223 GB/s）可能与新硬件本身同样重要。带宽有所帮助，但容量依然是那堵墙。

TPU Sync 采用 Apache 2.0 许可证，其代码仓库包含架构文档、C++ 和 Python API，以及单主机和多主机解耦服务与主机 KV 卸载示例。在稳定版本发布之前，JAX 和 PyTorch 软件包只提供开发版本，存储分层和强化学习权重同步功能也仍处于实验阶段。

items.title: Spanish PM and rivals rally supporters in final pitch for votes
items.content:
# Spanish PM and rivals rally supporters in final pitch for votes

Pedro Sánchez accused his opponents of hurling insults and lies but his conservative rival has promised a new era of politics

- Published

**Spain's main party leaders have held their final rallies ahead of Sunday's election, with Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez saying he is confident of defying the polls.**

"I cannot imagine us losing," he said, posing for selfies with supporters in red T-shirts and accusing conservative rival Alberto Núñez Feijóo of planning a coalition with the far right.

Feijóo's People's Party (PP) is narrowly ahead in the polls, and in the final hours of the campaign he travelled first to Barcelona and then Seville, promising voters a new political era of "truth, decency and good governance".

He accused Sánchez of evading questions on key issues like corruption, rail disasters, immigration and the national debt.

Alberto Núñez Feijóo's PP holds a narrow lead in the opinion polls

The Socialist leader heads one of Europe's few left-wing governments, and with the French presidential elections five months away, there is a real chance that two of the continent's biggest economies could move to the right in quick succession.

Almost 39 million people have a vote in Spain and while commentators expect a high turnout, most polls have suggested a close finish. Under Spanish electoral law, no polls have been published since Monday.

"This time, yes, we're going to do it," Feijóo told PP supporters, in a nod to his failure to form a government three years ago despite winning most seats.

Abascal said on Friday that Sánchez's government had 'betrayed' Spaniards

If he gets to form a government this time, it will be with the support of anti-immigration party Vox, led by Santiago Abascal, whose final rally took place in front of thousands of people in a bull-ring in Valencia on Spain's east coast.

The venue was filled with Spanish flags and green Vox banners, and one of the biggest cheers of the night came when the secretary general of the party called for "less burka and less halal".

Ignacio Garriga said he was not acting out of hatred but love for the homeland.

A small section of the crowd could be heard chanting "Viva Franco" in reference to the dictator, whose death in 1975 heralded the start of Spain's transition to democracy.

A number of first-time voters at the rally said they were supporting Vox because of its policies on immigration.

Lledó, 18, said what had happened in Ceuta in the summer, when more than 70,000 migrants crossed into the Spanish territory from Morocco, showed Sánchez was not able to control the country's border.

She had come to the bullring with her mum and aunt, Carli Chilet, who argued that Vox "are the best for women's rights".

Vox is hoping to almost double its seats from the 33 it won three years ago. It backs policies such as "national priority" - putting Spanish citizens first for welfare - and "remigration" for foreigners not considered to be contributing to the economy.

Lledó attended the rally with her family

- Leaders clash in final Spain election debate as housing dominates run-in
  - Published17 hours ago
- Spanish election: What you need to know and what's at stake
  - Published10 hours ago
- Who to watch in Spain's election race
  - Published11 hours ago
- Clashing political visions reflect a divided Spain ahead of election
  - Published2 days ago

The final day of campaigning was very much in the shadow of a four-way TV debate the night before that exposed Spain's sharply polarised politics.

All four leaders had solutions for the housing crisis. Feijóo said the PP would build a million homes over four years, while Sánchez said housing should be a right not an object of speculation and profit.

Watch: Could housing decide Spain's general election?

While the conservatives tried to turn the spotlight on the series of scandals that have overshadowed the Socialists' term in office, Sánchez and his left-wing ally Ada Colau, who heads Frente Amplio (The Broad Front), focused on women's rights.

The two leaders seized on a moment in the debate when the PP leader accused Colau and the rest of the left of staying quiet during a flood disaster in Valencia, briefly moving his finger to his lips. The word he used "calladita" is a diminutive and can also be used to tell a woman to "keep quiet" in a condescending manner.

Sánchez reacted immediately and called on him to show "a little respect", accusing him of sexism.

Feijóo sought to clarify what he meant on Friday, and accused Ada Colau of remaining silent during "these years of corruption". His decision to wind up his campaign in Seville was significant, because the wider southern region of Andalusia has 61 seats in Spain's 350-seat parliament, more than any other.

Andalusia is also important because it is run by a coalition made up of the PP and Abascal's Vox, as are three other regions, Extremadura, Aragón, and Castilla y León.

Feijóo has insisted he wants to govern with a majority, backed up by "parliamentary support agreements" with Vox and says he has never spoken to Abascal about giving Vox ministerial power.

"Governing is about managing, and I have spent my whole life preparing for this moment," he said in Seville.

One of his new supporters at the rally was a retired woman called Isabel who told Spanish public broadvaster RTVE that she was attending a PP rally for the first time. The formerly loyal Socialist voter said she was "disillusioned" with a party led by Sánchez. Another voter at the rally said Spain needed "a good manager".

Colau is a former mayor of Barcelona

Sánchez took to the stage in Madrid with his wife Begoña Gómez, and donned a red T-shirt that read "power of the people".

He then went on to praise Colau and her left-wing coalition's campaign.

"These elections are about moving Spain forward, not taking it backwards," he said.

Socialist supporter Leon Felipe, 25, told Reuters news agency: "Well, I think what's at stake in these elections is a big deal, is not a change of government... but rather a return to the past - a return to Franco's dictatorship.

"So, I believe that young must mobilise."

As he was speaking, Colau told a large audience in the south of Madrid that not only would they "not remain silent, we will win", vowing to form another "progressive government".

items.title: JetKVM Mini W Review A Simple and Small Wireless External KVM Device
items.content:
We have been testing the JetKVM Mini W (and the wired Mini) for some time, and it is time for a review. The Mini W’s “W” stands for wireless, since it connects to the network wirelessly. Another neat part about this is the price. At $42 each, these are inexpensive for what they offer. Despite being inexpensive, this did not feel “cheap.” We will get into why in the review along with some things we would want to change, and some bits that were executed very well.

## JetKVM Mini W Hardware

The box itself is roughly 1.7″ x 1.7″ x 0.9″, so it is really small. If you need to put a KVM in a bag, this is great. Also, the chassis is mostly aluminum, so it is small but feels premium, whereas you almost expect something small and inexpensive to be plastic and cheap.

The screen on this little box is useful and is a big plus versus something like the GL.iNet Comet GL-RM1. The screen shows us a PIN for setup and can show you the IP address of the KVM. A small bummer is that it is not a touchscreen, so you navigate the menus with two side buttons.

Another challenge is internal storage for mounting ISOs and such. Here, you get a TF card slot, so you can add a microSD card for local storage (Amazon Affiliate). That adds about 50% of the unit’s cost, so we understand why JetKVM left it out, but having Ubuntu, Proxmox VE, and our custom AgentSTH ISOs loaded on it is super useful.

On the side, we get to buttons to navigate the menus.

Then comes the most important side with two USB Type-C ports and an HDMI port. We have an early unit that came from JetKVM, but clearly these need to be labeled. On the website, the ports have labels.

The left Type-C port (as shown below) is for the connection to the managed system. The center Type-C port is for power input.

We got two Type-A to Type-C cables to provide both data and power connections for the unit.

Finally, the HDMI port is for HDMI input from the managed system.

We got a little HDMI cable as well.

Next, let us get to the software setup.

## JetKVM Software Setup

This is one of the more interesting ones. Since you do not have a wired network port, you cannot get a DHCP address. Instead, JetKVM’s website uses a local phone or PC/ Mac to pair with the device.

Then, you can set up the WiFi and find the IP address for the unit.

Once that is complete, you can navigate to the IP address and finish setup.

There are a few steps you can complete, but one interesting one is that you can use a password or passwordless login.

Overall, the setup process was easy once you realize you need to pair the unit to set it up.

Next, let us get to the interface.

items.title: 'We couldn't give up that easily': Marching bands scramble to cover costs after Thanksgiving parade rearranged
items.content:
# 'We couldn't give up that easily': Marching bands scramble to cover costs after Thanksgiving parade rearranged

How New York reacted to postponement of Macy's parade

- Published

**Since New York City officials postponed the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade, a precaution ahead of a storm that brought heavy rain, wind and flooding, hundreds of touring performers who traveled from across the US to perform were thrust into chaos.**

"It was jarring," said Ryan Demkovich, director of a Texas high school marching band. After learning the news, he had to scramble to make new arrangements for over 500 people.

Demkovich and his Pearland High School band made the quick decision to launch a fundraiser, reaching $350,000 (£267,000) in just a few hours.

Still, some performers reportedly had to skip the parade, a televised, traditional Thanksgiving event - now rescheduled for Saturday.

On Wednesday afternoon, a day before the event, organisers announced the postponement, in part due to concerns around the parade's giant balloons in strong winds.

The balloons, inflated on Wednesday, were then temporarily deflated - along with the spirits of those who journeyed to the city to watch the action.

The move represented the first time the event had been postponed in its 100-year history, although it was suspended altogether during World War II.

Each year, a number of marching bands travel from across the country, from high schools and colleges, to perform at the event. This is considered a huge opportunity, as the parade is watched by millions in person and on TV.

- Macy's postpones Thanksgiving parade due to severe weather
  - Published1 day ago

Demkovich described an emotional and exhausting experience, first learning that the parade would be postponed while watching a Broadway performance of Wicked with his band.

"My initial thought was like, 'Oh, crap. We're not going to be able to go'," he said.

"Where are we going to be able to get all the money for this?"

The delay meant unexpected expenses of additional nights in a hotel - and meals - for hundreds of people in the middle of New York City during the holidays.

There were no vacancies to extend their stay at the New York Marriott Marquis in Times Square, so they booked the nearest hotel with availability - across the Hudson River - in New Jersey.

Demkovich said the Pride of Pearland Marching Band posted a fundraiser online and within hours met its fundraising goal.

"The word just spread like wildfire, truly like wildfire," Demkovich said, adding that donations came from over 2,000 people and local businesses.

He called the outpouring of support "very, very overwhelming to think about and comprehend".

"We have a lot to be thankful for this Thanksgiving."

Some groups were not able to maneuver as easily. The University of Alabama's Million Dollar Band is one of those missing out, due to a schedule conflict on Saturday.

“‘This can’t be happening’,” Rina Browder, mother of a snare drummer in the band, told local news, describing the band’s reactions.

"They were devastated. They've worked so hard for this. So many practices."

The Pride of Pearland Marching Band from Texas - pictured rehearsing earlier this week - said it raised hundreds of thousands of dollars

Meanwhile, a group from Hawaii, the Nā Koa Aliʻi Hawaiʻi All-State Marching Band, said it too would still be able to participate in the parade, also because of emergency fundraising by families, friends and other supporters donating more than $500,000.

Speaking to the BBC on Thursday, the group's director Rickey H Badua described the time pressures. "We are racing to get this done," he explained.

The band is made up of hundreds of musicians from dozens of schools across the state. It travelled almost 5,000 miles (8,000km) to get to New York.

"Getting the news that we got the parade postponed was not easy, and emotional for our students," Badua said.

But the musicians sprang into action quickly, he said. "We come from a very far place," Badua said, adding that "to get so close to the finish line and not show up for it, we couldn't give up that easily".

The response from friends and family had been "incredible", he said.

New York City mayor on postponing 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade

Badua was hopeful his group would have the same experience he had when he first performed at the parade in 2003, as student drum major.

"The energy is palpable, people are just excited to see a band that is great."

Another musical act, from Illinois, told the BBC on Thursday it needed to raise $175,000 to cover another night in a hotel, additional food, and bus costs back to the city of Champaign.

"Things are going well due to the very generous support of so many amazing human beings," said Professor Barry Houser, director of the University of Illinois Marching Illini.

By Friday, 3,500 donors had stepped up to help the 410 students and their travel party. "This is truly phenomenal," said Houser.

While awaiting the parade, musicians and punters alike have sheltered from the heavy wind and rain brought by the storm to eastern areas of the US.

Hundreds of thousands of homes were without power in the storm's aftermath Friday, and coastal areas had flooded. The National Weather Service (NWS) expects conditions to improve gradually on Friday.

*Additional reporting by Jessica Murphy*

导语：投资方包括励石、商汤国香、长石、厚雪、险峰长青、磐霖等多家机构。

“AI算力的成本中心正在从‘计算’转向‘连接’。”

雷峰网(公众号：雷峰网)·鲸犀独家获悉，MicroLED 高速光互连芯片与光引擎研发商「闪科光联」近日完成数千万元人民币天使轮融资。

种子轮由励石创投独家投资，天使轮由商汤国香、长石资本、厚雪资本联合领投，险峰长青（K2）、磐霖资本、小苗朗程、柯熙创投等多家产业基金共同跟投。

鲸犀进一步获悉，闪科光联成立于 2026 年 9 月，创始人周秋桂博士毕业于美国弗吉尼亚大学，师从“全球 APD 之父” Joe C. Campbell 院士，回国后任职于华工科技，并从零组建了硅光团队。

此后，周秋桂共同参与创立了熹联光芯，主导光电融合这一新架构的落地与量产。从经历来看，周秋桂完整走过了两代光互连技术的产业化。

团队上，闪科光联的核心技术团队来自华为美研所、美国高通、华工正源等企业，在光电芯片、先进封装、高速光模块领域拥有 20 年以上经验。

据周秋桂等闪科光联人士透露，公司以 MicroLED 光互连技术为核心，瞄准 AI 算力基础设施中“连接比计算更贵”的结构性瓶颈，致力于为下一代数据中心、AI集群和超算中心提供低成本、低功耗、高带宽密度的新一代互连方案。

这项技术的可行性正在被海外巨头验证，如何快速工程化落地并走向量产正是闪科光联聚焦的方向。

周秋桂对鲸犀判断称，AI 算力的天花板，过去由单颗芯片的性能决定，焦点在芯片里面，未来则取决于芯片集群之间的较量，核心在芯片与芯片之间。

“重新定义这层光互连的上限，与中国光电子产业一起，把这场技术变革的主动权握在自己手里。”周秋桂表示。

据雷峰网·鲸犀了解，本轮天使轮融资资金将主要用于核心芯片研发、封装样品线建设。公司已同步启动下一轮融资，将加速推进 MicroLED 光互连产品的工程验证与量产导入。

items.title: Canada's top court largely upholds Quebec ban on religious symbols for public servants
items.content:
# Canada's top court largely upholds Quebec ban on religious symbols for public servants

- Published

**Canada's top court has largely upheld a Quebec law banning public sector workers from wearing religious symbols, including the hijab and the cross.**

The law, known as Bill 21, faced legal challenges from a range of groups, including female Muslim, Sikh and Catholic teachers, who argued it violated their fundamental rights.

Quebec passed the law in 2019 under a unique fixture of Canada's constitution called the "notwithstanding clause" - a legal loophole that allows governments to override certain rights, like freedom of religion.

The Supreme Court's decision is one of the most closely watched in Canadian history, with an impact that will be felt both in Quebec and across the country.

Reacting to the ruling on CBC, Prime Minister Mark Carney said his government would study its implications, adding it was important for all legislatures "to respect the rights and liberties of all Canadians, including those in the minority."

The Supreme Court was asked to weigh in on a number of questions, including on the constitutionality of Bill 21, whether Quebec's use of the notwithstanding clause was appropriate, and whether there are limits to its use.

On Friday, the top court confirmed the validity of Bill 21, but ruled that the law infringes on democratic rights by banning Quebec's elected officials from wearing a face covering for religious reasons.

The court also ruled that a Canadian court has the power to declare whether a law is consistent with the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms even if the notwithstanding clause is invoked, but that they would not do so in this case.

While the majority of the seven justices found that Quebec's law is largely valid, some dissented to parts of the decision.

Justices Andromache Karakatsanis, Michelle O'Bonsawin and Nicholas Kasirer wrote that the notwithstanding clause "cannot be used to authorize laws that are incompatible with the fundamental character of Canada as a free and democratic country".

Specifically, they said they believe the law infringes on the charter's guarantee to freedom of religion, freedom of expression and the right to equality.

- What to know about the Supreme Court decision on Quebec's secularism bill
  - Published4 hours ago

Civil liberty groups in Quebec have criticised Bill 21, saying it disproportionately affects Muslim women who wear the hijab, arguing that it has excluded them from key areas of public life in the province.

Stephen Brown, CEO of the National Council of Canadian Muslims, called the law "discriminatory" and criticised the court's decision.

"Entire categories of people are now barred from entire sectors of employment, not because of what they have done, but because of who they are," he said.

The chair of the English Montreal School Board, one of the main groups challenging the law, said the board was "obviously very disappointed" with the ruling.

"It wasn't the result we were looking for," Ortona told reporters. "But we do take solace from a lot of the declarations that were made by the court."

Quebec has argued that the law is necessary to uphold the province's state secularism - or laïcité - as a core component of its identity.

Earlier this year, the province passed another bill expanding its secularism rules to subsidised daycares and post-secondary institutions. It also restricted public prayer with fines for non-compliance.

The leader of the Bloc Québécois, a federal party that advocates for Quebec sovereignty, said Friday's ruling upheld the province's right to protect its values.

"We are now more than ever in a position to move forward with the preservation of the very elements that profoundly define the distinct nature of Quebec society," Yves-François Blanchet told reporters in French.

Watch: Isolation or neutrality: The cost of Quebec's secular law

items.title: TSMC Reveals Details of A14 Manufacturing Compared to N2P
items.content:
TSMC has revealed additional technical details about its upcoming A14 (1.4nm-class) manufacturing technology at the 2026 Europe OIP Ecosystem Workshop, providing semiconductor designers with a clearer picture of the performance, power efficiency and density improvements expected from its next-generation process.

The company also announced that version 0.9 of its A14 process design kit (PDK) is ready for customer design activities, representing an important milestone toward commercial production.

A14 is scheduled to enter risk production in the second half of 2027, followed by high-volume manufacturing in the second half of 2028.

###### Second-Generation Nanosheet Transistors

A14 represents TSMC’s second generation of gate-all-around (GAA) nanosheet transistor technology, building upon the foundation established by its N2 family.

Unlike FinFET transistors, GAA nanosheet transistors allow the gate to surround the channel, providing improved electrostatic control and greater flexibility in transistor design.

TSMC is also introducing NanoFlex Pro, an evolution of the NanoFlex standard cell architecture used in its N2 process family. NanoFlex Pro provides designers with additional opportunities to optimize power, performance and area (PPA) according to specific application requirements.

An important innovation is the introduction of Boost Cells and Low-Power Cells. Designers can deploy Boost Cells along performance-critical paths while utilizing Low-Power Cells in portions of the design where maximum operating frequency is less important.

This flexibility allows engineers to improve overall chip efficiency without imposing the power and area penalties associated with optimizing every circuit for maximum performance.

###### A14 Compared to N2P

According to TSMC, A14 with NanoFlex Pro delivers approximately 14% higher performance at equivalent power or a 23% reduction in total power consumption at equivalent performance compared with N2P using NanoFlex.

TSMC also presented the following comparisons against baseline N2P technology.

The results illustrate how transistor innovations, physical design improvements and standard cell optimization are increasingly working together to deliver meaningful generational advances.

Importantly, the energy-efficiency figures against baseline N2P use a different comparison from the performance and power figures against N2P with NanoFlex.

###### SRAM Scaling and Design-Technology Co-Optimization

SRAM scaling has become one of the most difficult challenges associated with advanced semiconductor manufacturing.

TSMC’s upcoming A14 technical presentation at IEDM describes an SRAM bit cell measuring less than 0.017 square micrometers.

This advancement is particularly important for AI processors and high-performance computing devices, which increasingly incorporate large amounts of on-chip cache and embedded memory.

Design-technology co-optimization (DTCO) is becoming essential as traditional geometric scaling delivers diminishing returns.

By simultaneously optimizing transistor structures, standard cells, interconnects and physical design methodologies, foundries can extract additional value from each manufacturing generation.

###### EDA Ecosystem Readiness

Another significant announcement is the readiness of the A14 design ecosystem.

Both Cadence and Synopsys have completed full design-flow certification using an Arm Cortex-A725 CPU core, covering implementation and signoff methodologies. Siemens EDA is also progressing toward additional certifications.

Early ecosystem readiness reduces customer adoption risk and enables semiconductor companies to begin development well ahead of manufacturing availability.

TSMC is also providing customers with a migration path from A14 to A13, which is scheduled for volume production in 2029 and is expected to offer approximately 6% die area savings without significant changes to the existing design flow.

###### Why It Matters

A14 arrives at a critical time for the semiconductor industry.

AI accelerators, data center processors and mobile computing platforms are increasingly constrained by power consumption, thermal management and manufacturing economics rather than transistor performance alone.

Even modest improvements in energy efficiency can translate into substantial operational savings when deployed across hyperscale AI data centers.

A14 could also intensify competition among the world’s leading advanced foundries, particularly as Intel develops its 14A technology and Samsung advances its own GAA manufacturing roadmap.

Ultimately, TSMC’s A14 strategy demonstrates that the future of semiconductor scaling depends on the integration of manufacturing technology, transistor architecture, design optimization and EDA ecosystem readiness.

**Bottom line:** The next era of Moore’s Law will increasingly be defined not simply by smaller transistors, but by how effectively the entire semiconductor ecosystem works together.

- TSMC — Q2 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

items.title: AWS Challenger: Trainium3 Inference and Microarchitecture Deep Dive
items.content:
The Nvidia GPU was originally built to shade pixels, and every Nvidia generation since 2017 has bolted on another piece of AI-specific hardware to fix the bottleneck the previous one exposed. Volta added Tensor Cores, Hopper added TMA for tile data movement between HBM and SRAM, and Blackwell added Tensor Memory for accumulating. Nvidia removed many hardware units that are required to render graphics for their datacenter GPUs

In comparison, the Trainium microarchitecture is built ground-up specifically for ML workloads, with tiles as a first-class primitive instead of having a sea of threads and then bolting on tensor/tile compute and data movement engines. Trainium3 behaves the way the physics says it should. In this past this meant software was a humongous challenge, but now no longer.

7 months later, Trainium 3 and TPUs are live on InferenceX, both trading blows or even winning vs Nvidia GB300 in cost to generate tokens at TCO. We will dive into those details below.

This advantage is not purely due to Amazon’s ultra low cost supply chain. It's also due to microarchitectural decisions, which we will dive into in this post. For example, using the Trainium Descriptor Generation Engines (DGE), the equivalent of Nvidia TMA and AMD MI455X TDM, our microbenchmarks show that Trainium can reach peak HBM bandwidth utilization (MBU) at small message sizes, which is not possible on Nvidia GPUs.

Furthermore, our testing covers cycle-level SRAM scratchpad latency and bandwidth testing (SBUF to PSUM), rack-scale bandwidth and latency microbenchmarks, attention exponential testing, and the precise cycle-level latency of different shapes, including how different attention head\_dim (K) would affect the percentage of roofline.

Every result comes from UBenchX, our microbenchmark suite, and we model each unit from first principles before we measure it. We thank Nafea Bshara (Co-Founder of AWS Annapurna Labs), Ron Diamant (Trainium Chief Architect), Michael Shteinbok, Armin Ebrahim and the rest of their team for helping teach us their architecture and validate our benchmark experiments.

Star the InferenceX & UBenchX GitHub repository if you find the open-source benchmark and data useful! InferenceX is the only inference benchmark in the world to have TPUv7, OpenAI Jalapeño, Nvidia Rubin NVL72, AMD, and now, Trainium3.

# Trainium’s Superior Inference Performance per Dollar - AgentX

AgentX measures Trainium3 on a production end-to-end agentic inference workload. This is achieved by replaying real coding-agent sessions against a Trainium3 server. The goal is to compare accelerators’ *realistic* inference performance, that you may expect to see on actual agentic workloads.

For those unfamiliar with InferenceX, the Pareto frontiers (curves) represent the fundamental inference tradeoff between throughput and latency. Each point is a different inference configuration targeting a different latency-throughput target. At each slice of the x-axis, higher perf per TCO is better and directly leads to higher inference gross margins.

Today, we are excited to share that Trainium 3 PDS + vLLM achieves amazing perf/$ TCO across the entire frontier. In fact, it is better than every other accelerator besides Vera Rubin across the *entire* TCO versus p90 interactivity curve. This is an amazing achievement.

Trainium is also very competitive from an end-to-end latency perspective, across the entire curve. With that being said, there is still room for improvement, particularly with respect to TTFT.

It is not surprising that Trainium lags behind in some p90 TTFT cases against GB300 as this metric is largely dictated by prefill, a compute bound operation. Trainium3 has only 17% the theoretical FP4 flops as Blackwell Ultra (2,517 TFLOPS versus 15,000 TFLOPS). It has more competitive interactivity since decode is memory bound and Trainium3 has 4.9 TB/s per chip against 8.0 TB/s for GB300, 61% of the bandwidth at about 30% the TCO. Also, pipelined prefill (which Trainium relies on, as discussed in the subsequent section) generally favors throughput over latency.

In fact, at a p90 interactivity of 135 tok/s/user (a typical speed you’d observe on OpenRouter), Trainium3 with vLLM yields the highest profit margin at 73.5%, compared to runner up GB300 + SGLang at 53% (at 3 year rental prices). This assumes Z.ai list price for token pricing and a 60% hardware fleet utilization factor.

Trainium3 achieves these margins with 144GB of HBM per chip, half GB300’s capacity per GPU. This reflects our Short King thesis: additional HBM capacity must deliver enough extra throughput at the target latency to justify its cost. This is also why 4-Hi is attractive industry wide option and next generation accelerators are primarily using 8-Hi.

What makes these results interesting for this article is how directly the software follows the hardware we measure in Section 2. Prefill and decode run on separate nodes, and each arranges the same 16 chips to suit the topology.

## Prefill

A quick primer for this section: a Trainium3 chip has 8 NeuronCores, each pair sharing one HBM stack, and a node is 16 chips. Section 2 covers the hardware in detail. For a more in depth analysis, see our Trainium3 deep dive article.

A prefill node is a pipeline. The model’s layers are cut into 16 stages, one chip per stage, and a chunk of prompt tokens flows from chip to chip. Inside a stage, the chip’s 8 NeuronCores split the chunk between them, so all of the stage’s tensor and expert parallelism stays on one chip.

This is the layout our collective benchmarks argue for. Chip-level collectives were well ahead of every wider group we tested, and all-to-all, the pattern MoE layers need, is slower once it leaves the chip. With the heavy exchanges kept on one chip, what limits a stage is TensorE, which is where the MXFP4 matmul modes covered below do their work.

## Decode

For decode, one copy of the model is spread across individual ranks on all 128 NeuronCores (across 16 chips), and every core takes part in the computation for each token. For those familiar with Nvidia architecture, each GPU is typically a separate rank whereas Trainium treats all 128 cores as logical devices and separate EP ranks. In the case of multi-user GLM-5.3, this assigns two routed experts per NeuronCore. Decode runs at LNC=1, so each physical NeuronCore is its own rank, whereas the rest of this article uses the default LNC=2.

Again, each NeuronCore is its own device with local HBM, so nothing synchronizes across the chip unless the software invokes a collective. Nvidia added locality domains in CUDA 13.4 to pin Rubin kernels to one die’s memory in the same way.

Not every exchange spans the node though. Decode declares nested groups of cores: half a chip, one chip, the two chips of a tray, two trays, half the node, and the whole node, plus a second family that takes the same core position on every chip. The smaller exchanges, such as the dense layers and the shared expert, can run on the small groups. A group of 8 is one chip and a group of 16 is one tray, whose two chips share a direct link, so those exchanges never touch a switch. But activations are gathered across all 128 cores and the expert outputs are reduced across all 128, so that traffic crosses the switch on every layer.

# Trainium Profiler Fine-grain Accuracy - Better Than Nvidia and AMD

Trainium’s profiler is by far the industry leader and is state of the art (SOTA). Trainium’s profiler is loved by all the performance engineers at Anthropic. Anthropic’s head of performance has publicly said that performance analysis on Trainium is way better than performance analysis on Nvidia GPUs (and obviously better than on AMD GPUs). In order to demonstrate how fine-grained their profiler is, we recreated the Olympic performance of the Bay Area’s own Alysa Liu on the actual Trainium3 hardware profile. We were mainly inspired by the Bad Apple post from Daniel Liu (Anthropic Performance Engineer). This combines fine art, performance art, and chip architecture all into one video.

Full video:

# Section 2: Microbenchmarks

## Hardware and Programming Model

Trainium3 consists of 8 NeuronCore-v4s, and every 2 NeuronCores share an HBM stack. By default, 2 NeuronCores that share an HBM stack form a Logical NeuronCore (LNC). Users write kernels that map to LNCs, and in LNC=2, it follows the Single-Program Multiple-Data (SPMD) paradigm: NeuronCores in an LNC execute the same kernel program with separate hardware resources except the HBM. In a Neuron Kernel Interface (NKI) kernel, programmers can assign work to NeuronCores in an LNC with the API nl.program\_id and synchronize NeuronCores with the barrier mechanism nisa.core\_barrier.

One of the most important concepts in data movement is **the partition dimension** (pdim) and **the free dimension** (fdim). Every tensor has a designated partition dimension, and other dimensions are called free dimensions. In principle, the partition dimension aligns with the dimensions of hardware components, and data can be processed in parallel. We explain the dimensions of each component throughout the article.

## Memory

### HBM Bandwidth

Here we investigate the achievable HBM bandwidth of Trainium3. In Trainium3’s memory hierarchy, we move data from HBM to SBUF using the API nki.isa.dma\_copy. Each NeuronCore comes with 16 main Direct Memory Access (DMA) engines, in charge of moving data between HBM and SBUF. For every data transfer, a main DMA engine ingests a DMA descriptor, which contains the source and destination address information. In Trainium3, there are three modes of generating DMA descriptors: static (None), software-based DGE (swdge), and hardware-based DGE (hwdge). Each mode generates and stores descriptors differently.

Starting from NeuronCore-v3 (Trainium2), GpsimdE comes with one integrated DMA engine per processor, totaling eight integrated DMA engines. With these integrated DMA engines, programmers can perform data movements in parallel with the main DMA engines, while also enabling indirect access patterns, such as gather and scatter operations. NeuronCore-v3 also comes with two Descriptor Generation Engines (DGE). DGE accelerates descriptor generation with hardware: it frees up GpsimdE to perform other computation, frees up memory space, and accelerates address generation. DGE resembles Tensor Memory Accelerator (TMA) in Nvidia architecture and Tensor Data Mover (TDM) in AMD architecture. TMA focuses on accelerating large data copies at the cost of higher latency, while hardware-based DGE has no performance trade-offs compared to software DGE. However, while TMA is able to perform gather and scatter operations, not even the latest NeuronCore DGE can do so. As a result, NKI constrains DMA copy mode to swdge when performing indirect memory accesses.

Here we compare the achieved memory bandwidth of a single Trainium3 NeuronCore for the three descriptor modes. Static mode, since descriptors are compiled ahead of time, has the lowest descriptor generation overhead and achieves the highest memory utilization. At the smallest tested message size 64 KiB, static mode achieves 492 GB/s (80% utilization) for load and 544 GB/s (88.8% utilization) for store. Static mode also achieves near peak memory bandwidth at around 256 KiB. Hardware DGE, the default mode of DMA copy, follows closely behind static mode: it achieves 398 GB/s (65% utilization) for load and 476 GB/s (77.7% utilization) for store at 64 KiB message size, likely due to the address generation overhead. The gap narrows as message size increases, and hardware DGE mode matches static mode after 256 KiB. On the other hand, software DGE performs significantly worse than the other two. This likely indicates indirect memory access patterns may suffer great performance loss, as they are restricted to software DGE mode.

Trainium3 consists of 8 physical NeuronCores, and while they have individual DMA engines, each pair of NeuronCores shares one HBM stack. Thus, we measure the memory bandwidth achieved by 8 concurrent NeuronCore programs to understand the utilization under full load. Overall, the HBM is able to sustain the high utilization, dropping by only about 3% for larger message sizes.

### PSUM to SBUF Bandwidth

In Trainium3, PSUM and SBUF are arranged in a 2D grid of 128 lanes of 16 KiB / 256 KiB capacity. The 128-lane setup is the partition dimension, and the data is accessed in parallel along the partition dimension.

There are two main types of data movement between PSUM and SBUF:

- SBUF to PSUM: Upon an nki.isa.nc\_matmul call, TensorE moves both input matrices from SBUF to PSUM
- PSUM to SBUF: Epilogue operations such as data type casting, activation, and quantization. These operations are mostly based on the nki.isa.tensor\_copy API

This section focuses on PSUM to SBUF. Two engines have PSUM read access: ScalarE and VectorE. We measure the achieved memory bandwidth for the two engines across different tile shapes, using the full 128 partitions with varied per-partition sizes.

Our results show that PSUM read bandwidth starts from 453.9 bytes per cycle for ScalarE and 413.9 bytes per cycle for VectorE at 32 KiB message size, and both reach near the theoretical bandwidth of 512 bytes per cycle (4 bytes per cycle per lane, 128 lanes) at around 256 KiB message size. This translates to a 614.4 GB/s bandwidth for each engine. Starting from NeuronCore-v3 (Trainium2), the two engines can perform PSUM reads in parallel. Our benchmarks show that parallel access causes near-zero bandwidth loss, indicating that the PSUM is well designed to sustain parallel access. When both engines are used in parallel, they reach 1024 bytes per cycle.

The bandwidth gap between the two engines in the smaller message sizes indicates different instruction issue overhead: ScalarE has about 8 cycles of overhead, whereas VectorE has about 16 cycles.

## Tensor Engine

Tensor Engine (TensorE) is the hardware unit that executes matrix multiplications. In terms of architecture, TensorE is a systolic array, which consists of a 128-by-128 processing element (PE) grid. The 128 dimension matches the number of partitions in SBUF and PSUM, and since TensorE reads both matrix inputs from SBUF and writes the results to PSUM, this simplifies programming. TensorE applies near-memory accumulation: the output accumulates in PSUM, avoiding a round trip to HBM, and it is especially useful for epilogue operations and consecutive matrix multiplications. This design is also present in Nvidia Blackwell, where the TensorCore output accumulates in TMEM.

We invoke TensorE with the API nisa.nc\_matmul. For a matrix multiplication of x @ y = z, the input dimensions are as follows:

- Stationary x.T: \[K, M\]. Maximum of M (stationary fdim) is 128; TensorE reaches full performance at K=128
- Moving y: \[K, N\]. Maximum of N (moving fdim) is 4096. This is because PSUM has 16 KiB per partition, which can hold a maximum of 16384 B / 4B = 4096 FP32 elements
- Output z: \[M, N\]

Note that TensorE requires the stationary matrix x to be transposed, meaning the hardware takes x.T as input but computes x @ y. This is due to TensorE’s systolic array design: the systolic array computes dot products between rows of x and columns of y.

### Simple Systolic Array Performance Model

In the systolic array, each y column is staggered by one element. Every TensorE matrix multiplication involves two steps: LoadStationary (LS) loads the stationary matrix into the array, and MovingMultiply (MM) performs the calculation. During each cycle of MM, every PE computes a partial sum, passes the y element to the PE on its right, and passes the partial sum to the PE below.

With the understanding of the systolic array, we can model the instruction latency as N+254 cycles. In a matrix multiplication, the lower-right element is the last to complete computation, and it depends on how many cycles it takes to move the lowerleft element of y into the lower-right PE. Focusing on the dynamics of the lower-left element of y, we see there are three stages: fill, stream, and drain. The fill stage refers to the period when the input edge isn’t full due to staggering, which is R-1 cycles, where R represents the number of rows in the PE grid. The stream stage refers to the last row entering the PE grid, and it takes N cycles for the lower-left element to reach the input edge. Finally, the drain stage is when the PEs consume the moving matrix inputs, and it takes C-1 cycles for the lower-left element of y to get to the lower-right PE, where C represents the number of columns in the PE grid. Overall, the latency is (R-1)+N+(C-1)=127+N+127=N+254 cycles.

We can also model the initiation interval as approximately N cycles for sufficiently large N. Initiation interval is the time gap between instruction launches when we consecutively launch many of the same instructions. In this case, we model the number of cycles between a series of MM instruction launches. From the perspective of the systolic array, we can continuously stream multiple input matrices y1, y2, … in the same staggered fashion, and the computation of the next MM instruction starts as soon as the next input matrix’s element streams into a PE. In a steady state where we ignore the fill and drain stages, each PE streams through one row of input matrix y for every MM instruction, meaning the initiation interval is N cycles. However, this only holds for large N due to our steady-state assumption.

## nisa.nc\_matmul Performance

We collect experimental results to verify our modeling. We are able to map the latency results to the formula N+393 with little error, indicating that there’s a roughly 140-cycle overhead for MM instructions, which may include things like writing results to PSUM.

As for the initiation interval, experiments show that by adding a constant 6-cycle overhead, we are able to reliably predict the initiation interval for matrix multiplication shapes N >= 64 and M=128. As we suspected, the model breaks down for small N, and we observe the initiation interval to be 30 cycles at N=8, likely dominated by other overheads.

Our model also predicts that M is irrelevant to both performance metrics, and our experiments corroborate this. At N=512, both latency and initiation interval stay constant across all M sizes. This has great implications for performance. LLM inference decode workloads tend to have small M for matrix multiplications, and M not being the main factor in performance alleviates many difficulties when optimizing decode workloads.

We also measure a more realistic scenario, where we change both stationary and moving matrices, so the kernel alternates between executing LS and MM instructions, and the two instructions of different matrix multiplications can overlap. Results show that we reach more than 90% utilization at N=64, and we reach near theoretical throughput for shapes larger than N=128.

## Double FP8 Matmul Performance

Starting from NeuronCore-v3 (Trainium2), TensorE supports FP8 matrix multiplication. In terms of programming, users set the argument perf\_mode to nisa.matmul\_perf\_mode.double\_row, and double row mode supports contraction dimension K=256, 2x the standard K=128. However, the systolic array is still a 128-by-128 PE grid, so under the hood, double row mode shards the input into two tiles along the K dimension and computes them in parallel. During computation, each PE takes in two FP8 elements from the moving matrix and computes two multiply and accumulation operations every cycle.

As a result, the latency of FP8 double row mode is near-identical to its BF16 counterpart, and we show this in the experiments below. TensorE can theoretically double the throughput of FP8 matrix multiplication, since the latency is still bounded by the same systolic array grid. In reality, we see FP8 demonstrating near-identical instruction latency and initiation interval as its BF16 counterpart.

However, for realistic scenarios of alternating LS and MM instructions, double\_row mode FP8 performance is mixed. When comparing the same shapes, FP8 underperforms BF16 until around N=96 and only reaches 2x the compute throughput after around N=256, which makes sense as FP8 is executing at half the N size. If we consider the effective N size, double row mode FP8 only starts showing throughput benefits at N=64.

FP8 power throttles more frequently than its BF16 counterpart, indicating that typical performance may be less ideal than our full-rate measurements.

## Microscaling Matmul Performance

NeuronCore-v4 (Trainium3) introduces microscaling format (MXFP4, MXFP8) matrix multiplication support with the new API nisa.nc\_matmul\_mx.

### Quad-MX Matmul

Further scaling the FP8 matrix shape, nc\_matmul\_mx supports the K dimension of 512 (4x the standard) through the quad-MXFP8 data type. Users pass the matrices into the API nisa.quantize\_mx to compact the matrices along the K dimension, packing every 4 MXFP8 elements into one quad-MXFP8 element, resulting in the K to be 128. Trainium3 offloads the quantization step to the user, instead of TensorE doing it, and this is different from major MX-supporting hardware such as Nvidia and AMD GPUs. This reduces the quantization overhead during the matrix multiplication instruction but exposes the quantization step to users to optimize.

With the quad-MXFP8 data type, how LS loads the stationary matrix and how MM streams the moving matrix behave closer to the standard nc\_matmul, except each element is 4-bytes wide. nc\_matmul\_mx accepts quad-MXFP8 inputs and theoretically has the same performance characteristics as the BF16 nc\_matmul, hence 4x the throughput. Realistically, quad-MXFP8 does have similar latency and initiation interval as BF16 nc\_matmul, but still suffers from minor overhead, which is understandable given the dequantization step. As for computation throughput, quad-MXFP8 outperforms its BF16 counterpart for most shapes, but it only reaches 4x throughput for N greater than 128.

### Row Tiling Mode

Row tiling mode is another new feature in NeuronCore-v4 (Trainium3) unique to nc\_matmul\_mx. Row tiling mode allows users to concurrently execute multiple matrix multiplications with smaller K dimensions, improving the utilization of TensorE. TensorE achieves this by splitting up the systolic array along the rows and outputting the results without passing down the partial sums through the whole array. Row tiling mode offers multiple configurations, including tile sizes (32, 128) and (64, 128). A tile represents the cut-up systolic array, so tile size refers to the number of quad elements, and the packed K dimension is essentially the partition size, which we denote as Kp.

Theoretically, row tiling mode should offer T times throughput, where T represents the number of tiles. Here we compare the un-tiled, the tiled, and the standard full array configurations.

Our results show that row tiling mode does improve utilization and achieve higher throughput, and it reaches near the theoretical 2x / 4x boost for N >= 128. Compared to the standard full array configuration, row tiling mode retains about 90% of the full array throughput and closes the gap at N=512. A caveat of row tiling mode is that it might not support certain shapes due to PSUM capacity limits, since the number of output matrix elements doubles / quadruples.

## Full Chip Performance and Power Throttling

We further investigate the power throttling effects on TensorE performance by benchmarking with full chip activated, specifically, 8 matrix multiplication kernels on 8 NeuronCores in a chip. We compare all data types, including BF16, double row FP8, MXFP8, and MXFP4, and we run at the (M, N) = (128, 512) for a typical shape with max K size for each data type.

Overall, we see BF16 executing at near max compute throughput, double row FP8 and MXFP4 running at around 90% MFU, and MXFP8 heavily throttled at 68.6% MFU. To set up a non-power throttled comparison, we use AWS power profile tools to apply a clock-limited profile, lowering the max boost clock from 2.4 GHz to 2 GHz. As shown below, all precisions except MXFP8 reach near the max throughput of 2 GHz rate, but are throttled at around 80% of the original MFU. For MXFP8, it reaches 84.5% MFU of 2 GHz rate, boosting the true MFU at 1.9%. This shows power throttling is a critical issue for the MXFP8 matrix multiplication using TensorE.

# Transcendental Functions

Transcendental functions are the math operations used in model activations, and those operations are critical to kernel performance due to their inherent mathematical calculation complexities. By default, ScalarE computes the transcendental functions, and to program ScalarE, we call nisa.activation and pass in the math operation, e.g. nl.gelu, as argument. Starting from NeuronCore-v4 (Trainium3), other engines support small sets of the transcendentals. For example, GpsimdE supports functions like sigmoid, and VectorE supports the exponential function through the new API nisa.exponential.

We first benchmark the exponential function, since the exponential function throughput is a great performance bottleneck to FlashAttention operation. Here we compare VectorE and ScalarE to find out how much VectorE boosts the performance. The benchmark setup follows the most common softmax precisions, FP32 input / BF16 output and BF16 input / BF16 output. According to documentation (here and here), both engines have 128 compute lanes, matching the partition dimensions of PSUM and SBUF. For each cycle, ScalarE executes at 1 element per cycle, while VectorE at 2 FP32 elements / 4 BF16 elements per cycle. We sweep through different free dimension sizes while keeping partition dimension to 128, and the element process throughput is as below.

Benchmarks show that ScalarE and FP32-input of VectorE quickly nears the theoretical throughput at around fdim=256, while it takes fdim=1024 for BF16-input to get to near 512 elements per cycle. As for instruction latency, ScalarE saturates quickly at fdim=16, after which latency scales with fdim, whereas VectorE saturates at fdim=64 for FP32 inputs and fdim=128 for BF16 inputs.

nisa.exponential API offers many features relevant to FlashAttention, including subtract by max value for stable softmax, and input summation for running exponential sum calculations. We are delighted to see such ergonomic improvements.

We further benchmarked activation functions commonly used in LLMs. All activation functions surprisingly perform identically, reaching near max 128 elements-per-cycle performance at fdim=256.

# Intra-Logical NeuronCore Communication

Trainium supports grouping 2 physical NeuronCores into one Logical NeuronCore (LNC). Physically, an LNC maps to two NeuronCores that share an HBM stack. Physical NeuronCores within an LNC have two ways of communicating: exchanging data on SBUF through DMA engines and accessing the shared HBM with a semaphore mechanism.

nisa.sendrecv implements the bi-directional data exchange, and it’s essentially a two-rank all-gather operation. sendrecv supports utilizing the main DMA engines and the ones in GpsimdE. sendrecv through GpsimdE (GpSIMD DMA) offers lower latency but has message size restrictions. Our benchmark shows GpSIMD DMA achieves up to 2.6x lower latency at a small message size of 512 bytes, but the speedup diminishes as message size increases, and the two transfer methods cross over at 32 KiB. For the main DMA engine, the latency greatly increases after 128 KiB message size, and the bandwidth nears saturation at 14 MiB, reaching 572 GB/s. We couldn’t increase the message size without errors, which is likely due to the SBUF size being 32 MiB.

Neuron also supports the all-reduce version, nisa.sendrecv\_compute, where we pass in an NKI operator, and the NeuronCores perform a fused all-gather and reduce operation. Here we compare a naive sendrecv + tensor\_tensor add setup with sendrecv\_compute add. We see minor improvements for smaller message sizes but performance loss at large ones.

The shared HBM pattern is an all-gather that uses nl.shared\_hbm to access the shared HBM and nisa.core\_barrier to synchronize the NeuronCores. Both NeuronCores write their tiles from their own SBUF to the shared HBM, wait for the semaphore, and copy each other’s tiles from the shared HBM to their own SBUF. To understand the semaphore mechanism overhead, we also benchmark a local copy for a comparison.

Overall, the core barrier semaphore introduces 10-20% latency overhead. Compared to shared HBM + semaphore, sendrecv is the more performant option for doing 2-rank all-gather operations, as sendrecv skips HBM and transfers from SBUF to SBUF.

The latency curve shows a peculiar dip around 8 KiB, and we investigate the reason. We hypothesize that the dip is due to the partition size matching the HBM burst write size. Smaller sizes trigger frequent read-modify-write operations, which adds to latency. On the other hand, data transfer time dominates latency for larger sizes.

Partition size, rather than message size, appears to be the cause. When we hold the message size constant and vary the number of partitions and partition size, the latency drops 2-3x between partition size 16 bytes and 32 bytes.

Sweeping through partition sizes for the 128-partition configuration, we see latency drops for partition sizes that are multiples of 32. This implies the HBM write burst may be at 32 bytes.

## Inter-LNC Collective Communications

Neuron supports LNC-level communication, from intra-chip to full UltraServer, through the collective communication APIs nki.collectives. Using the Neuron collective benchmark nccom-test, we tested the major collective operations, including all-gather, all-reduce, reduce-scatter, and all-to-all.

## Intra-Chip LNC Collective Communication

For intra-chip LNC, the NKI collectives API supports two types of data transfer source and destination: HBM to HBM and SBUF to SBUF. For the HBM-to-HBM collectives, we see the achieved bandwidth for all operations plateau at around 256 MiB message size and hold it up to 4 GiB. Which algorithm runs depends on Neuron’s collective algorithm selection. Neuron intra-node collective communications documentation says Neuron chooses different algorithms for different message sizes: Mesh for small message size, Recursive Doubling Halving (RDH) for medium, KangaRing for large, and Ring for backup.

On one chip, all-gather uses Mesh up to 2 MiB and RDH from 4 MiB. All-reduce, reduce-scatter and all-to-all stay on Mesh at every size we tested.

SBUF to SBUF (sb2sb) collectives allocate the input, output, and buffers on SBUF instead of HBM. sb2sb avoids round trips to HBM, which is advantageous for communication-computation overlapped kernels to reduce latency. In our testing, we found sb2sb runs up to 24 MiB for all-gather, reduce-scatter and all-to-all, and up to 16 MiB for all-reduce, despite SBUF being 32 MiB in capacity; we believe the intermediate steps of collectives may require extra memory. Currently, sb2sb performs on par with HBM-to-HBM up to about 2 MiB. Above that, all-to-all stays on par, while the other three operations flatten and HBM keeps climbing. However, Amazon engineers are optimizing sb2sb collectives, and we expect the performance to rapidly improve in the future.

## Cross-Node Collective Communications

To show the scalability of Trainium3 on collective operations, we benchmarked the major collective operations with four world sizes: 1 chip (4-rank) as the baseline, 1 node (64-rank), 1 rack (128-rank), and 1 UltraServer (256-rank). We see chip-level collectives significantly outperform other world sizes, achieving roughly 1.5x to 3x the bandwidth at sizes below 16 MiB. The other three configurations perform similarly, with the 1-node setup performing slightly better at smaller message sizes. This shows the rack is designed to scale well without losing performance. For all-to-all, chip-level achieves about 9x to 10x the bandwidth of node and rack-level world sizes, meaning performing all-to-all within a chip is highly advantageous.

**We will further test this in CollectiveX, which runs more complex, realistic collective patterns and will publicly launch in a few weeks.**

We compare the 2-node collective operation performance of different link types, including intra-rack NeuronLink, cross-rack peer NeuronLink, and cross-rack non-peer EFA. Overall, we see the NeuronLink types perform roughly the same, and intra-rack only visibly outperforms cross-rack at message sizes of 256 MiB and above. If we compare NeuronLink with EFA, NeuronLink types achieve about 1.65x the bandwidth. All-to-all is the unique case here: only intra-rack NeuronLink supports 128-rank all-to-all, while EFA supports a limited 2-rank 64-group all-to-all. Intra-rack NeuronLink reaches a max of 31 GB/s, while cross-rack non-peer EFA can only reach 8 GB/s.

## Trainium3n

In our AWS Trainium3 Deep Dive article, we explained the different network architectures of the Trainium3 NL32x2 Switched. We run all of our benchmarks on a Trainium3 NL32x2 Switched on gen1 switch trays, but in this section, we present the collective operation benchmark results of Trainium3 NL32x2 Switched on gen2 switch trays, comparing it with its gen1 counterpart.

Gen1 uses 160-lane Astera Scorpio X switches to connect 32 chips in a rack, and the lane count constraints lead to a dual switch plane design. On the other hand, gen2, labeled as Trainium3n (trn3n) in AWS documentation, employs 320-lane Astera Scorpio X switches, and 8 switches form a single switch plane to connect all chips in a rack. Dual switch plane means some chips in a rack are two hops apart (a switch hop plus a tray link), whereas a single switch plane puts every chip in a rack one switch hop away. This theoretically lowers latency for node-level, rack-level, and UltraServer-level communications, and we show the experimental results below.

At large message sizes, the Trainium3n design also raises bandwidth across all collective operations. Most notably, Trainium3n achieves a 2.8x bandwidth for all-to-all, which is very helpful to mixture-of-experts model workloads.

Latency tells the same story at small message sizes, where the time per operation is mostly fixed cost and not bandwidth. The largest gain is at rack level: on Trainium3n, a collective across the two nodes of a rack costs almost the same as one inside a single node for all-reduce and reduce-scatter, while gen1 pays a clear step for leaving the node. This is the removed switch hop showing up directly. The gain carries through to the full UltraServer, where both operations run about a fifth to a quarter faster than on gen1.

All-to-all improves modestly at node and rack level. The only cross-rack all-to-all that runs is between two non-peer nodes in small 2-rank groups over EFA, and there the two generations are identical, at about three times the in-rack latency.

# Intra-Chip and Scale Up Cycle Latency and Bandwidth Topology

## Intra-Chip NeuronCore to NeuronCore

A Trainium3 chip is 2 dies of 2 SENGs each. A SENG, short for “shared engine”, is two NeuronCores sharing one HBM stack, so a chip has 8 cores and 4 stacks. Each core also has its own SRAM: SBUF for a kernel’s working tiles and PSUM for matrix-multiply partial sums. An HBM stack serves only its own pair of cores, so the pair never competes with the others for memory bandwidth. The cost is four separate HBM domains per chip: data needed outside its SEngine has to be moved by a DMA copy or a collective.

In the core-to-core exchange latency/BW diagram, we can see transfers within SENGs being faster, and cross die being slowest, due to no diagonal links.

## Node Level Cycle Latency and Bandwidth Topology

As we covered in our previous Trainium3 article, the two chips in a tray are linked directly, and trays are joined through two switch planes per rack: one for the even-numbered chips and one for the odd-numbered chips. Traffic between an even chip and an odd chip in different trays therefore takes an extra hop, which shows up as a checkerboard pattern in the chip-to-chip matrix.

Newer racks use a single-plane design instead, where one switch plane connects all 32 chips in the rack. These use the Gen2 PCIe switch trays, removing the checkerboard pattern.

items.title: 德语媒体：习近平清除了一名潜在继任者
items.link: https://www.dw.com/zh/德语媒体：习近平清除了一名潜在继任者/a-80077870?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.content:
# 德语媒体：水泥浇筑的债务

《经济周刊》评论写道，房地产危机爆发五年之后，其连锁反应仍在拖累中国经济，看似繁荣的出口业也仅只能起到缓冲作用。《新苏黎世报》分析文章指出，随着中共上海市委书记陈吉宁的落马，习近平又清除掉一名潜在的继任者。

（德国之声中文网）《经济周刊》评论写道，房地产危机带来的影响远不止家庭财富缩水，众多的中国地方政府也陷入了严峻的财政困境，曾经支撑城市经济腾飞的土地经济模式，早已成为历史。这篇题为《水泥债务》的评论写道：

“过去几十年以来，土地买卖一直是中国城镇的重要收入来源。政府将土地开发权卖给开发商，只要不断有新的小区建成开售，政府就有了源源不断的财政收入。2021年，土地买卖收入达到峰值时，中国地方政府的这一项收入高达8.7万亿元，而2025年时，这项收入已经下跌了一半还多，而且仍在继续下跌。

土地收入锐减之所以会成为严重问题，是因为许多城镇在房地产火爆时期欠下了巨额债务。他们通过自家的借贷机构大量融资，用来修建道路、桥梁和工业园区，而这些债务一直没有在常规预算中得到体现。根据国际货币基金的估算，中国地方政府的显性和隐性债务总额已经相当于中国国内生产总值的90%。最令地方政府难堪的是，卖地收入大幅下跌的同时，以前的债务仍要继续还本付息，能用于公共投资的钱越来越少，那些靠地方政府项目过活的公司也越来越难以维持。

有鉴于此，北京当局也在想方设法，试图缓解地方政府的财政危机。例如，政府开始向部分首次购房者提供房贷利息补贴，此举既能缓解买房者压力，也能为地方政府提供一些喘息空间。而为了直接减轻地方政府的负担，中国政府还在2024年11月推出了一项债务转型计划，即以利率较低的债卷替代利息极高的隐形债务。今年10月，北京又允许地方政府新举债务5500亿元。不过，中国分析师郭涛（音）则表示：‘这一举措可以降低风险，赢得时间，但却填补不了土地收入留下的缺口。’”

《经济周刊》的评论指出，为了广开财路，地方政府也是各显神通: 税务部门开始追缴富裕人士的海外资产，监管部门开出的罚单也变得越来越多。但问题在于，企业和家庭所面临的经济压力越大，提振他们的投资和消费热情也就越难：

“现在，北京已经将发展重点放在电动车、半导体、机器人以及人工等智能领域，并在国际市场上取得了巨大成功，而新兴企业也确实给地方政府带来了新的税收。但咨询公司欧亚集团（Eurasia Group）中国主管王丹则认为，对国际市场的依赖也暗藏着新风险，‘获取如此之高的附加值，完全要依赖世界其他地区的需求’。她认为，中国政府的这种经济模式追求的就是贸易失衡，并已经引起了欧盟等贸易伙伴的强烈抵制。有鉴于此，重振地方财政，刺激出口并非长久之计。

更何况，房地产市场目前还看不到任何复苏迹象。住房供应现在就已严重过剩，而随着人口的不断减少，住房需求也只会进一步下降。经济学家王丹认为，房地产危机的余波还将持续数年，‘我们认为，房地产危机还将持续至2030年底。’”

《新苏黎世报》评论分析文章写道，中共上海市委书记陈吉宁曾被很多人视为习近平的潜在接班人，而新华社寥寥数语的短讯，就宣告了他政治生涯的终结：

”明年，中共将召开21大。一般认为，习近平届时将会开启其第四个为期五年的总书记任期。2018年，他已经取消了国家主席的两届任期限制。

目前没有任何迹象显示，现年73岁的习近平会指定接班人。相反，像陈吉宁这样私下里被视为潜在接班人的高层官员，其被清洗的风险反而会徒然增高。而随着这位上海市委书记被清洗，在习近平无法履职的情况下，谁来接替就变得更加不确定了。在指定接班人的问题上，习近平越拖延时间，留给接班人熟悉政务、巩固地位的时间也就越少。一旦大权在握的习近平突然离世，一场混乱的权力斗争恐怕将在所难免。

对习近平来说，忠诚高于一切，中国人民解放军就是一个明显的例子。中国军队的首要任务是保障共产党的权力，其次才是抵御外敌。外国军事观察家们普遍认为，持续不断的清洗行动已经削弱了中国军队的作战能力，而军官们也为了避免成为清洗目标，不愿做任何决定。

对习近平来说，军官们对党，也就是对他本人的忠诚度，要比他们的军事能力更为重要。他在讲话中也一再强调忠诚和反腐对他来说至关重要。”

items.link: https://www.dw.com/zh/大众卖给中国？德顶级经济学家抛出困境-解方/a-80076955?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.content:
# 大众汽车出售中国？德国经济学家争议言论引发轩然大波

2026年11月27日
德国基尔世界经济研究所所长舒拉利克在柏林一场工业会议上语出惊人：他建议德国可考虑将陷入困境的大众汽车出售给中国企业，并直言德国在汽车领域已沦为“发展中国家”。这番言论在会场引发骚动，也折射出欧洲汽车产业在中国竞争压力下日益深重的战略焦虑。

（德国之声中文网）德国基尔世界经济研究所所长舒拉利克（Moritz Schularick）再次发表针对大众汽车集团的争议性言论，认为德国可考虑将陷入困境的大众汽车集团出售给中国企业，并直言德国在汽车产业的部分领域已沦为“发展中国家”。

据德国《商报》（Handelsblatt）报道，舒拉利克周二在柏林举行的一场工业会议上表示：“如果我们趁沃尔夫斯堡的某家企业还能卖出价钱时，把它卖给中国人，这并不是一个坏主意。”

他强调，从德国的角度来看，最重要的是确保“价值创造和生产活动继续留在德国”，至于这些生产设施最终归谁所有，则是次要问题。这番言论在会场引发一阵骚动。

近年来，大众汽车不仅在中国市场持续流失份额，在欧洲也面临中国竞争对手的激烈挑战，目前正通过削减成本等措施推动业务重组。

舒拉利克同时呼吁欧洲采取更强硬的政策措施。他认为，欧洲应允许中国汽车进入当地市场，，但同时也应该采取措施，促使中国企业将生产活动转移至欧洲。他举例称，政府可以将“欧洲制造”（Made in Europe）作为获得补贴的条件、要求成立合资企业等措施，促使中国车企在欧洲设厂生产。

他指出，中国过去也曾对欧洲企业采取类似政策, 德国如今必须认清现实：“在这些领域，现在我们才是发展中国家。”

（商报）

相关专题：德国汽车工业

items.title: Intel Foundry: How Better Power Delivery Could Unlock More AI Performance
items.content:
An AI accelerator can have more transistors, more memory bandwidth, and a faster interconnect, yet still leave performance on the table if its power delivery network cannot keep up. Intel Foundry’s white paper Driving Power Delivery Innovations for the AI Data Center Era makes an optimistic case for what comes next. Engineers can shorten the path electricity takes to the transistors, put more stored charge near the circuits that need it, and move voltage conversion closer to the compute die. Together, those changes could help future accelerators make better use of the power they draw.

###### The challenge starts with current

AI accelerators operate at low voltages, so supplying more power means delivering more current. Intel’s paper puts package currents in the multi-kiloamp range for highly integrated designs. Resistive losses rise with the square of current, which makes long delivery paths increasingly costly. Sudden jumps in demand can also cause a brief drop in supply voltage. Designers may compensate by raising the operating voltage enough to maintain stability through those dips, increasing energy consumption in the process.

That challenge grows as compute chiplets and high-bandwidth memory share a package. The routing and surface area needed to supply power are also needed for high-speed connections, and each die can have different voltage and current requirements. Intel Foundry’s approach gives designers several places to act, from the silicon itself to the package and the voltage regulator.

###### Shorter paths and steadier voltage

PowerVia, introduced on Intel 18A, routes power through the back of the die while leaving frontside wiring available for signals. Shorter current paths reduce resistive voltage drop, and separating the two networks eases routing congestion. That gives designers more freedom to improve power delivery and signal routing independently. Intel plans to build on that approach with PowerDirect on Intel 14A.

The paper also describes how to handle the moment an accelerator suddenly needs more current. Capacitors close to the active circuitry supply charge while the regulator catches up. Intel’s Omni MIM uses vertical trenches to fit more capacitance into a given area on the die. Embedded capacitors add charge storage inside the package, where surface space is scarce. EMIB-T, meanwhile, adds vertical paths through the silicon bridge connecting dies, so current can take a more direct route through a densely packed design. These changes matter as packages bring compute and memory closer together and have to supply both within a limited footprint.

Voltage conversion offers another opportunity. Moving the regulator closer to the compute die shortens the distance that low-voltage, high-current power has to travel. Intel’s continuous capacitive voltage regulator, or C2VR, uses capacitors in place of inductors and can be thinned to less than 100 micrometers for potential placement beneath a compute die. Intel reports a 92% peak conversion efficiency for the research design cited in the paper. The placement is as interesting as the efficiency figure. Bringing conversion directly under the load creates a shorter vertical path and helps the regulator respond quickly when demand changes.

###### Why it matters beyond the package

Data centers have a finite amount of power and cooling capacity to allocate. At the same facility power budget, an accelerator that loses less energy between the voltage regulator and the transistors can leave more of that budget available for computation. Lower distribution losses also mean less heat from the power delivery network itself. Over many accelerators, even modest gains can affect how much compute fits within a rack’s electrical and thermal limits. The size of those gains will depend on the accelerator, its workload, and how the package is built.

The foundry opportunity is to give chip designers a choice about where to make those gains. A high-current logic die may benefit most from backside delivery. A package crowded with memory and chiplets may have more to gain from embedded capacitors or a bridge that carries power vertically. A stacked design could benefit from placing a regulator directly beneath the compute die. Having those options makes power delivery a design decision architects can make alongside transistor technology, memory bandwidth, and packaging. For AI and high-performance computing, that opens a path to higher performance by getting more useful work out of the power already available.

**Source:  Intel Foundry, Driving Power Delivery Innovations for the AI Data Center Era.**

Why Intel’s EMIB Matters for Microsoft Azure

Intel’s Tiny Bridges Could Lead to Very Big Paychecks

How AI is Reshaping Semiconductor Design and Manufacturing
